purpose: A machine-readable UI system description extracted from the workspace so another LLM can reproduce the same design language across new apps without collapsing Anan into a generic dashboard theme.

approach.important_note: Anan is not one flat style. It is one brand DNA expressed through multiple surface families: workspace web, public marketing, public docs, private docs, client assistant, mobile buyer, shared AG-UI cards, and admin.
approach.reproduction_rule: Choose the correct surface family first, then apply the shared brand DNA and only that surface's geometry, spacing, and tone rules.

brand_dna.platform_context: Anan is a multi-party real-estate infrastructure connecting buyers, brokers, developers, operations, and AI assistance.

house_look_and_feel.summary: Quiet premium utility. The UI prefers pale structural surfaces, blue signal accents, dark ink text, crisp borders, Cairo-heavy typography, and measured motion. It should feel like a serious workspace, not a theme demo.
signature_contrasts: deep slate ink against nearly white surfaces
one strong electric/institutional blue used as the focal signal
large, confident Cairo headlines paired with muted operational labels
soft neutrals for surfaces with hard, intentional information hierarchy

primary_signal.role: core Anan highlight across workspace, marketing, client web, docs, mobile, AG-UI, and most admin surfaces
usage: brand signal lines and motion artwork

ink.role: main dark text / icon color family used in public, mobile, and many structured panels

workspace_ink.role: workspace bubble-other foreground and richer informational ink

neutral_system.rule: Most interfaces are built from disciplined slate/zinc neutrals; blue is reserved for emphasis, not background flooding.

docs_private_light.accent_style: hard bordered white cards with strong category colors instead of soft glassy tints

mobile_native.cursor_card_frame_behavior: ambient background edge fade to transparent

radius.reading: The system uses compact 8px-ish primitives for general web controls, then large 18px-32px radii for premium cards, assistant bubbles, and mobile surfaces. Full pills are extremely common for chips and primary actions.
radius.llm_rule: Do not standardize everything to one radius. Match the surface family: compact web controls use 8-12px; premium panels use 24-32px; chips and primary utility CTAs often use full pill radii.

typography.font_strategy: Cairo is the default voice across workspace, marketing, docs, client web, mobile, and admin. Geist Mono is reserved for code/technical contexts.
weight_bias: font-bold for operational labels and strong body
font-black for headings, eyebrows, badges, CTA labels, and key figures

tracking_bias.rule: Eyebrows, badges, small labels, and institutional nav text frequently use uppercase and wide tracking. Headline/value text usually uses tight tracking.

case_rules.arabic_text: Keep natural Arabic case and prioritize rhythm/weight over forced caps.
case_rules.english_microcopy: Often uppercase in labels, eyebrows, nav, and CTA text.
case_rules.mixed_language_ui: Arabic content may coexist with English uppercase labels; this is acceptable if hierarchy remains clean.

borders.default_rule: Borders are a major structural device. The system uses low-contrast borders constantly to separate surfaces instead of relying only on shadow.
common_styles: 2px border for internal docs and certain marketing/public treatments

shadow.philosophy: Shadows exist, but are restrained and secondary to borders.
shadow.common_pattern: Soft, low-elevation shadows on premium cards and floating controls; many surfaces remain effectively flat.
avoid: large soft drop shadows on every card

motion.philosophy: Motion should clarify state and add polish, never dominate the interface.
observed_patterns: subtle hover translate or border shifts
SVG signal-line loops on marketing visuals
timing_bias: 4s-6.5s for decorative looping motion in marketing
spring-based short feedback for mic meters and small dynamic indicators
motion.llm_rule: Use motion only where it communicates hierarchy, activity, or liveliness. Marketing can carry more ambient motion than workspace or docs.

universal_rules: Preserve the shared blue signal color as the main emphasis token.
Use Cairo as the default face unless a technical/code context explicitly calls for mono.
Prefer slate/zinc neutrals and white surfaces over tinted UI backgrounds.
Build hierarchy with weight, tracking, spacing, and borders before adding decoration.
Let surfaces breathe with generous padding instead of stuffing density into every container.
Use RTL-aware alignment for Arabic-first experiences; do not assume LTR.
Keep illustrations vector-led, diagrammatic, or signal-based rather than stock-photo dependent.
Assistant UI should feel operational and trustworthy, not like a toy chat app.
Forms, cards, tables, and tabs should look like part of one system even when their radius differs by surface.

workspace_web.style_summary: Quiet premium dashboard shell with neutral zinc/slate surfaces, soft borders, compact top nav, assistant-first panels, and selective blue signal emphasis.
layout_rules: Shell uses sidebar + top navbar + content column.
Sidebar is pale/light in shared workspace mode; zone sidebar may switch to dark mode for deep contextual focus.
Content areas often use full-height, overflow-aware shells.
Cards and shells rely on borders and low-elevation shadow.

top_nav.shape: compact rounded action group on the trailing side
top_nav.actions: locale, theme, notifications, inbox, org switcher, user avatar
top_nav.tone: panel on panel, not loud chrome

sidebar.active_state: blue fill or blue-tinted border depending on context

message_chrome.user_bubble: dark slate or workspace self-blue bubble; compact rounded asymmetry
message_chrome.assistant_message: often transparent or pale surface with rich markdown formatting
message_chrome.badge_row: pill badges above assistant message showing assistant/team routing

composer.style: large rounded translucent/glass-like white shell with light blur
composer.send_button: dark filled circle when text exists

brand_subsystem.section_frames: simple white bands with bottom borders and strong headings
brand_subsystem.vector_panels: inline SVG signal artwork with gradient wash and blue/slate/emerald accent variants
brand_subsystem.stat_strips: grid strips with shared frames and strong values

component_rules: Tabs are usually border-bottom based, not underlined with heavy decoration.
Filter chips use rounded-xl or pill geometry with high-contrast active state.
Empty states use dashed borders, large radius, centered icon/initial badge, and muted copy.
AG-UI cards use 26px radius, workspace-panel background, workspace-border, and soft shadow.
do_not: Do not turn workspace into a bright blue dashboard.
Do not add rainbow analytics color unless chart semantics require it.
Do not use generic chatbot gradients or neon AI glows.
Do not flatten all cards to 8px radius; premium assistant and workspace cards are noticeably rounder.

marketing_public.style_summary: Editorial institutional landing style with strong Cairo display type, explicit section bands, vector motion artwork, white/slate/dark section alternation, and clean blue CTA accents.
layout_rules: Use large, deliberate vertical rhythm: common section padding is 24-32 units.
Alternate section backgrounds between white, pale slate, dark slate, blue, and glass/gradient variants.
Keep a large max width around 1400px for major sections.
Use centered or split two-column storytelling layouts.
hero_rules: Hero titles are extremely large and bold, often with one blue-emphasis line/segment.
Badge rows use tiny uppercase microcopy with wide tracking.
Descriptions frequently use right border accents in blue.
Primary CTA is blue fill; secondary CTA is outline or dark.
visual_language: Vector-led and signal-led, not product screenshot dependent.
Subtle looping motion via SVG overlays and floating movement.
Background textures are low-opacity grids or brand vectors, not generic blobs.
card_rules: Cards often use 2px borders, big padding, uppercase black titles, and minimal icon badges.
Variant set usually includes default, dark, and accent-blue.
tone_rules: Public pages can be bolder and more graphic than workspace.
Still avoid playful trend-driven visual gimmicks.

docs_public.style_summary: Polished technical-doc style: softened glass top nav, rounded cards, subtle shadows, blue semantic highlights, and clean dark mode.
rules: Top nav stays blurred, sticky, and low-noise.
Docs cards feel polished and slightly premium with mild shadow and rounded edges.
Endpoint and article navigation cards use rounded-2xl/3xl framing and slight hover lift.
Use blue for method accents, quickstart, active links, and informational callouts.

docs_private.style_summary: Sharper, stricter, more handbook-like than public docs. More visible borders, less blur, fewer rounded surfaces, more utilitarian editorial structure.
rules: Use harder borders and simpler white backgrounds.
Rounded-none or very low-radius elements are acceptable here.
Teal may appear as an internal-handbook action accent.
Top nav and callouts are more structural and less glossy than public docs.
docs_private.difference_from_public_docs: Public docs are polished and productized; private docs are intentionally stricter and more operational.

client_web.style_summary: Simplified assistant shell reusing the workspace token base but with lighter, friendlier conversational primitives and fewer enterprise chrome elements.
rules: Assistant bubbles are rounded-2xl, compact, and obvious in role contrast.
User messages use primary fill or dark fill; assistant messages use muted surfaces.
Suggestion chips are small outline pills with blue emphasis.
Structured advisory cards should remain clean and use workspace-border rather than introducing a new visual language.

mobile_buyer.style_summary: Arabic-first, Cairo-heavy, tactile, rounded, comfortable, and structurally calm. It is more intimate and pill-based than the web workspace.
interaction_rules: Everything must respect right alignment and RTL by default unless the content clearly starts in Latin script.
Primary actions often use full pills.
Conversation panels use rounded 24px-style containers with light borders.
Text hierarchy leans heavily on Cairo black for titles, chips, and prices.
Cursor-style property cards use an ambient edge fade so they feel embedded in the conversation surface.
Property cards should expose one explicit CTA and avoid action overload.
Privacy, session, or control states should be visible when they affect user expectations.
The mobile composer should stay calm at rest with one main prompt surface and a dynamic mic/send action.
mobile_buyer.special_mobile_note: The send button in the composer uses a warm orange (#E57B4B), which is a local interaction accent rather than a global brand replacement.
do_not: Do not port the mobile orange accent back into the general web brand.
Do not replace Cairo-heavy hierarchy with generic system fonts.
Do not turn mobile property shortlists into novelty carousels or stacked decks without an explicit product decision.

mobile_ai_conversation.role: Buyer-facing AI conversation rules for native mobile
mobile_ai_conversation.style_summary: Low-noise, trustworthy conversational UI with structured property cards, explicit control states, and calm React Native-native behavior.
rules: Assistant text should remain more open and typographic than user bubbles.
Structured cards should feel native to the current background through ambient adaptive fades.
Follow-up prompts should help the user move forward, not simulate personality.
Graceful failure and inline recovery are preferred over dramatic blocking states.
Avoid over-anthropomorphizing the assistant; escalation paths should feel supportive and task-focused.
When the user is still in normal chat flow, voice, send, and processing states should remain inline with the composer.

ag_ui_shared.role: Structured assistant UI cards shared across hosts
ag_ui_shared.style_summary: A host-aware card language built on workspace CSS variables so cards feel native inside the assistant shell.
rules: Use workspace CSS variables instead of hardcoded surface colors wherever possible.
Cards are content-dense but visually calm.
Common shell is rounded-2xl/26px, bordered, and softly elevated.
Headlines use black weight; support rows use elevated neutral containers.

admin_nexus.style_summary: A sharper, more assertive control-plane variant. It still belongs to the same family, but it pushes contrast, larger premium cards, and stronger dark-mode presence.
observed_rules: Primary buttons are often dark fills rather than blue fills.
Stat cards favor rounded 32px geometry with large numeric hierarchy.
Admin pages combine Cairo black typography with refined control-plane contrast.
Charts use an expanded semantic palette unavailable in most other surfaces.
admin_nexus.relationship_to_main_system: Treat admin as a sibling variant, not the default look for all new apps.

institutional_buttons.style: uppercase, high-weight, wide tracking, blue or dark fills, clean geometry

badges_and_chips.common_copy: micro labels often use font-black and wide tracking
badges_and_chips.inactive_pattern: white/slate surface with muted text and clear border

tabs.workspace_tabs: border-bottom active state, slim and editorial

empty_states.pattern: dashed border, soft neutral background, centered icon/initial, short strong title, muted support text

forms.workspace_and_admin: clean field framing, focus ring in blue, generous spacing, no busy helper chrome
forms.mobile: prioritize touch target, RTL alignment, and concise labels

chat.assistant_avatar: compact branded AI mark or sparkles, never generic bot emoji/iconography
chat.assistant_markdown: large line height, clean tables/blockquote treatment, blue markers
chat.user_messages: clear contrast and compact asymmetrical bubble geometry
chat.assistant_messages: more open and typographic, sometimes less boxed than user messages
chat.mobile_ai_cards: prefer one calm cursor-card shell with ambient adaptive fades, explicit CTA hierarchy, and visible control states when relevant
chat.mobile_ai_composer: prefer one calm multiline prompt surface, a dynamic mic/send action, and compact inline state banners

rtl.rule: Arabic-first surfaces default to right alignment and RTL writing direction; switch only when content clearly starts in Latin script or a technical/code context requires LTR.

contrast.rule: Default text contrast is high. Muted text is common, but important actions and figures should remain strong against pale surfaces.

selection_and_focus.focus: blue ring or ring-tint based on shared primary token
selection_and_focus.selection: blue-tinted selection background in shared globals

step_1_choose_surface: If building an authenticated operator dashboard or assistant workspace, use `workspace_web`.
If building a public landing/product page, use `marketing_public`.
If building external developer docs, use `docs_public`.
If building a buyer-facing assistant chat on web, use `client_web`.
If building a native mobile buyer/product app, use `mobile_buyer`.
step_2_apply_brand_dna: Keep Cairo as the default font.
Use blue as the main emphasis token.
Make hierarchy feel structured and premium, not playful.
step_3_apply_surface_geometry: Workspace: restrained shell, soft border, premium large-radius cards where needed.
Marketing: big type, bold sections, vector motion visuals, 2px structural borders in places.
Docs public: polished rounded editorial technical UI.
Docs private: stricter and more angular.
Mobile: pill-heavy, larger radii, Cairo-black hierarchy, RTL-first.
step_4_preserve_behavior: Prefer vector/system art over stock-photo dependency.
Keep AI surfaces calm and trustworthy.
On mobile AI surfaces, keep property cards vertical, ambient-aware, and action-focused.
output_requirements_for_new_apps: The generated UI should name and implement semantic tokens, not only raw Tailwind classes.
The generated UI should state which Anan surface family it belongs to.
The generated UI should preserve RTL behavior where relevant.
The generated UI should avoid introducing a new brand accent unless a local interaction reason exists.

do_not_rules: Do not reduce the whole ecosystem to one shadcn default theme.
Do not swap Cairo out for Inter, Roboto, or the system stack as the default face.
Do not replace the disciplined blue/slate/white palette with purple, neon cyan, or gradient-heavy branding.
Do not make every interface glassmorphic. Blur is occasional and controlled.
Do not overuse shadows. Border rhythm is more important.
Do not make admin, marketing, and workspace look identical; they are siblings, not clones.
Do not ignore RTL rules on Arabic-first surfaces.
Do not use whimsical AI mascots, chat gimmicks, or oversaturated sci-fi visuals.
